mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) relative to historical averages compresses equity discount rates, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without regime dependence.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) in periods where FEDFUNDS is below the 20th percentile of its historical distribution.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.3 percentage points over three months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) in instances where UNRATE rises by more than 0.3pp over three months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in consumer demand (RSAFS) and contraction in industrial output (INDPRO) indicates a supply-demand mismatch that triggers inflationary pressures and monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when RSAFS increases and INDPRO decreases simultaneously over the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes, a decline in housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 0.5% over one month signals an impending economic slowdown, generating negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) in late-cycle expansion periods when HOUST declines by more than 0.5% over one month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in monthly payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a robust labor market that supports corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days without regime dependence.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) in periods where PAYEMS growth exceeds the 75th percentile of its historical distribution.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) above 3.5% signals persistent inflation that triggers aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) in months where CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and decreases in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicate an overheating economy with aggressive monetary tightening, generating negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when FEDFUNDS rises and UNRATE falls simultaneously over the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: In supply shock regimes, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 1.0% over one month signals a contraction in manufacturing output, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) in supply shock periods when INDPRO declines by more than 1.0% over one month.
